MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. 1,250 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 125
   B. Ksh 12.50
   C. Ksh 13.50
   D. Ksh 1.25

2. Which formula gives the change from a purchase? (1 mark)
   A. Amount paid + total cost
   B. Amount paid − total cost
   C. Total cost − amount paid
   D. Total cost × amount paid

3. One unit costs Ksh 130. What is the cost of 6 loaves of bread? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 650
   B. Ksh 136
   C. Ksh 780
   D. Ksh 790

4. Two quarter turns together make (1 mark)
   A. a three-quarter turn
   B. a half turn
   C. a quarter turn
   D. a full turn

5. Kip faces North and makes a full turn. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. West
   C. South
   D. East

6. If you face north, which direction is on your right? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. South
   C. West
   D. North

7. Which of these is a right angle? (1 mark)
   A. The point of a sharp pencil
   B. A wide open gate
   C. The corner of a page in an exercise book
   D. A half-open pair of scissors

8. At 3 o'clock the hands of a clock make (1 mark)
   A. a right angle
   B. a very small angle
   C. a straight line
   D. a full turn

9. An angle that is bigger than a right angle has arms that are (1 mark)
   A. further apart than the arms of a right angle
   B. closer together than a right angle
   C. exactly the same as a right angle
   D. joined into one line and closed

10. How many corners does a triangle have? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 3
   C. 4
   D. 2

11. Which shape has no corners? (1 mark)
   A. Circle
   B. Triangle
   C. Rectangle
   D. Square

12. How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with no equal sides have? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 2
   C. 1
   D. 0

13. Which of these letters has a line of symmetry? (1 mark)
   A. F
   B. G
   C. H
   D. R

14. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. How many are NOT car? (1 mark)
   A. 10
   B. 1
   C. 11
   D. 9

15. What is data? (1 mark)
   A. Information that we collect
   B. A unit of time
   C. A kind of shape
   D. A measuring tape

16. The table shows the pets kept by 10 families: dog 3, cat 3, rabbit 2, hen 2. How many are NOT hen? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 9
   C. 2
   D. 12

17. In a tally chart, 2 groups of five and 4 more single tally marks are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 19
   B. 13
   C. 14
   D. 15

18. The table shows the pets kept by 10 families: dog 3, cat 3, rabbit 2, hen 2. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 10
   C. 12
   D. 9

19. Which of these is a good way to collect data on favourite games? (1 mark)
   A. Count the desks
   B. Guess what they like
   C. Ask each pupil which game they like best and record the answer
   D. Write only your own favourite

20. The table shows the vehicles that passed a school gate (10 vehicles): matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1. How many are matatu or lorry together? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 8
   C. 6
   D. 7

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Name three objects in your classroom that have right angles. (3 marks)

22. Explain why we add the numbers in the total row of a table. (3 marks)

23. Draw a triangle and write down its number of sides and corners. (2 marks)

24. Ten pupils were asked their favourite fruit and the answers were: mango, banana, mango, orange, banana, mango, pawpaw, mango, banana, orange. (a) Show the data in a tally table. (b) Which fruit is the most popular? (c) How many more pupils chose mango than orange? (5 marks)

25. At what times on a clock do the hands make a right angle and a straight line? Give one example of each. (4 marks)

26. Njeri faces east. She makes two quarter turns clockwise, one after the other. Which way does she face? (3 marks)

27. Name the plane figure of each object: a plate, a floor tile, a door. (3 marks)

28. State two things that are the same and two things that are different about a square and a rectangle. (4 marks)

29. Ten vehicles passed: 5 matatus, 2 boda bodas, 2 buses and 1 lorry. Draw a table to show this data. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Ksh 12.50
   1,250 ÷ 100 = 12 remainder 50, so it is Ksh 12.50.

2. B — Amount paid − total cost
   Change is what remains of the money paid after taking away the cost.

3. C — Ksh 780
   Cost = number × price = 6 × 130 = Ksh 780.

4. B — a half turn
   1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2, so two quarter turns make a half turn.

5. A — North
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. North followed by a full turn gives North.

6. A — East
   Facing north, east is on your right, west on your left and south behind you.

7. C — The corner of a page in an exercise book
   A page corner is a square corner, which is a right angle.

8. A — a right angle
   At 3 o'clock the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand at 3, a quarter turn apart.

9. A — further apart than the arms of a right angle
   A bigger angle has arms opened wider than a square corner.

10. B — 3
   A triangle has three sides and three corners.

11. A — Circle
   A circle has one curved edge and no corners.

12. D — 0
   No fold makes the two halves match.

13. C — H
   The letter H can be folded down the middle and the halves match.

14. D — 9
   10 − 1 = 9.

15. A — Information that we collect
   Data is information such as counts or names that we collect to answer questions.

16. A — 8
   10 − 2 = 8.

17. C — 14
   2 × 5 + 4 = 14.

18. B — 10
   Add all the numbers: 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 10.

19. C — Ask each pupil which game they like best and record the answer
   Asking and recording the answers gives real data.

20. C — 6
   5 + 1 = 6.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct, for example a window, a door and a book.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct object.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: To check that we have counted everything and that the total equals the number of items collected. If it is different we must count again.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for checking, 1 mark for comparing with the number collected, 1 mark for counting again.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: A drawing of a triangle with 3 straight sides. It has 3 sides and 3 corners.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the drawing and 1 mark for the numbers.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1 (total 10) (b) mango (c) 4 − 2 = 2 pupils
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for a correct table with title and headings, 1 mark for correct tallies and totals, 1 mark for (b), 1 mark for (c).

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Right angle: 3 o'clock (or 9 o'clock). Straight line: 6 o'clock.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for a right angle example and reason, 2 marks for a straight line example and reason.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: West
   Working / marking points: First turn east to south (1 mark); second turn south to west (1 mark); answer west (1 mark).

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plate: circle. Floor tile: square. Door: rectangle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct shape.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: Same: both have four straight sides and four right angles. Different: a square has all four sides equal and 4 lines of symmetry, but a rectangle has only opposite sides equal and 2 lines of symmetry.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for two similarities and 2 marks for two differences.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: A table with a title and two columns, Vehicle and Number, with rows matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1 and total 10.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for title and headings, 1 mark for all four rows correct, 1 mark for the total 10.
